cholera-second.name: Second cholera pandemic
cholera-second.says: Cholera spread from India across Western Asia to Russia, Europe, Britain and the Americas, and east to China and Japan, reaching Britain in October 1831.
cholera-second.toll: No overall total is given; the article describes hundreds of thousands of deaths in Europe, with local figures such as about 100,000 each in Russia and France and 6,536 in London.
cholera-second.open: The dates are not agreed (1826-1837 versus 1829-1849 or later), and the sources give no overall toll, only national and city counts.

covid-19.name: The COVID-19 pandemic
covid-19.says: Global pandemic of the coronavirus SARS-CoV-2, first detected in Wuhan, China, in December 2019; WHO assessed it as a pandemic on 11 March 2020 and ended the health emergency in May 2023.
covid-19.toll: As of 18 Sept 2026, 7.1 million confirmed deaths; modelled excess-death estimates run from 18.5 to 35.2 million. WHO put excess deaths in 2020-21 alone at 14.9 million (range 13.3-16.6).
covid-19.open: Official counts are widely held to undercount. Excess-death estimates differ by method and source, and the share caused directly by the virus is debated. The end date depends on the definition used.

dresden.name: Bombing of Dresden
dresden.says: British and American bombers struck Dresden in four raids from 13 to 15 February 1945, causing a firestorm that destroyed much of the city centre in the last months of the war in Europe.
dresden.toll: A historians' commission set up by Dresden city council (report 2010) found that between 22,700 and 25,000 people died in the British and US raids of 13-15 February 1945.
dresden.open: Whether the bombing was militarily justified or a war crime is still argued. Inflated tolls of 135,000 to 500,000 were spread by Nazi, East German and later far-right sources.
dresden.wiki: Bombing of Dresden in World War II

hiv-aids.name: The HIV/AIDS pandemic
hiv-aids.says: Disease caused by the retrovirus HIV, which passed from primates to humans in west-central Africa in the early to mid 20th century and was recognised as AIDS in 1981; it spread worldwide and continues.
hiv-aids.toll: At least 42.3 million deaths from 1981 to 2024 (Wikipedia); WHO's July 2026 fact sheet says 44.2 million to date. The two differ mainly by cut-off year; deaths continue, about 570,000 in 2025.
hiv-aids.open: Cumulative totals depend on the cut-off year and on modelled estimates, since death registration is incomplete in many countries. Wikidata lists earlier cumulative totals of 32 and 40.4 million.

holocaust.name: The Holocaust
holocaust.says: The systematic murder of European Jews by Nazi Germany and its collaborators, carried out by mass shootings in eastern Europe and by gassing at extermination camps, mainly in occupied Poland.
holocaust.toll: The Nazi German regime and its allies and collaborators murdered about six million Jews in 1941-45; the Wikipedia article gives 5.7 million as a conservative lower figure. Non-Jewish victims are counted separately.
holocaust.open: The six million is a rounded total built from several kinds of records; lower tallies near 5.7 million exist. Whether non-Jewish victims fall under the term Holocaust varies by author.

influenza-1918.name: The 1918 influenza pandemic
influenza-1918.says: Influenza A (H1N1) pandemic that spread worldwide in several waves from spring 1918 to 1920, infecting about a third of humanity, with notably high mortality among young adults.
influenza-1918.toll: Estimates run from about 17 million (a 2018 reassessment) through at least 50 million (CDC) to figures above 100 million; about 500 million were infected. Covers 1918-1920, worldwide.
influenza-1918.open: The global toll is uncertain by a factor of six, and the 17 million figure is itself contested. The name 'Spanish flu' is misleading: the place where it began is unknown.

jasenovac.name: Jasenovac concentration camp complex and Ustaša killings
jasenovac.says: Camps run by the Ustasa regime of the Independent State of Croatia, centred on the village of Jasenovac, held and killed Serbs, Roma, Jews and political opponents from August 1941 to April 1945.
jasenovac.toll: Recent scholarship and the US Holocaust Memorial Museum put deaths in the Jasenovac camp complex at roughly 77,000 to 100,000 across 1941-45; the memorial's named list is about 83,000.
jasenovac.open: Postwar Yugoslav figures ran from 500,000 to over a million; some Croatian writers gave 30,000-40,000. Cited sources note records were destroyed and numbers became politicised.

trail-of-tears.name: Trail of Tears
trail-of-tears.says: The US government forcibly moved about 60,000 Cherokee, Muscogee, Seminole, Chickasaw and Choctaw people from the Southeast to Indian Territory after 1830, with many dying of exposure, disease and hunger.
trail-of-tears.toll: Wikipedia's infobox totals 13,200 to 16,700 deaths across the Cherokee (4,000), Creek and Seminole (3,000), Chickasaw (3,500) and Choctaw (2,500-6,000) removals.
trail-of-tears.open: Counts vary by nation and source. Scholars differ on the label: some call it genocide, others ethnic cleansing, and one historian cited by Wikipedia says it falls short of genocide.
